description: Hi! I’m a high school student and the captain of Team Cupid. I’m interested in space, health, and technology, and I enjoy research, basic coding, and presentation design. I’m looking for teammates interested in programming, data analysis, biology, or UI design to help develop our astronaut health-monitoring prototype. Join me to share ideas, learn together, and build something meaningful—beginners are welcome!
summary:
We developed Cupid, an interactive web prototype that helps astronauts monitor and understand their cardiovascular health during space missions. It combines simulated heart rate, blood pressure, and exercise data with daily check-ins about sleep, fatigue, and symptoms.
Cupid addresses the challenge by turning health indicators into clear trends, comparing readings with a personal baseline, and helping users track assigned activities. Users can also download a summary for medical review.
Long-duration missions require astronauts to take greater responsibility for monitoring their health. Cupid demonstrates how an accessible tool could help them recognize changes and communicate concerns to medical professionals. Our prototype uses simulated data to demonstrate this workflow.
details:
Cupid is a web-based prototype designed to help astronauts understand cardiovascular changes during space missions. It brings health information, personal observations, and daily activities together in one easy-to-use interface.

Cupid aims to make health information easier to understand and help astronauts communicate changes to medical professionals. Our goal is to demonstrate a clear workflow: collect data, understand trends, follow an assigned plan, and review progress.

The dashboard displays simulated resting heart rate, blood pressure, exercise duration, and fatigue levels. Users can explore three scenarios: rising exercise heart rate, stable readings, and incomplete data. The app compares exercise heart rate with a simulated personal baseline at the same cycling workload, helping users understand why comparable conditions matter when reviewing health trends.

Cupid will be focused on health tracking and prediction. Based on the body data of astronauts, Cupid will give the best recommendation to help astronauts stay healthy and finish the task. When astronauts had some abnormal physical changes but they didn’t notice, Cupid would tell them immediately and change their daily schedule, such as sleep and exercise schedules.

Astronauts can also record sleep, energy, fatigue, and symptoms through daily check-ins. An action checklist demonstrates how they could follow a professionally assigned care and exercise plan. The progress page tracks completed activities and check-in history, while the Reports page lets users download a text summary for review.

We developed the prototype with assistance from ChatGPT, using HTML for structure, CSS for styling, and JavaScript for interactive features. Charts are drawn with SVG, and check-ins and checklist choices are saved using browser localStorage. A service worker supports offline access after the app has been successfully loaded and cached. No physical hardware was used.
